name: Suicide Hill (Colina del Suicidio), Jarama
story: On 12 February 1937, in the Nationalist offensive to cut the Madrid–Valencia road, the British Battalion of the XV International Brigade was thrown onto this knoll above the Jarama valley. For about seven hours it held against Moroccan Regulares and Legionaries supported by artillery and machine guns. Of roughly 600 men who went into action, only a fraction were still standing at nightfall; the writer Christopher Caudwell was among the dead. Neighbouring Dimitrov and Franco-Belgian battalions suffered similarly. The line bent but held, and the Jarama front froze here until 1939.
see: An open, olive-and-scrub hilltop with an informal stone cairn and plaques; traces of trenches and scattered shrapnel remain in the fields around.
plan: Morata de Tajuña publishes nine waymarked battle routes; route 7 starts here. Park carefully on the M-302 tracks; no facilities, bring water in summer.

boxes.text: Casualty figures for the British Battalion vary between sources (commonly 375 of about 600, or around 125 left unhurt of 400).
